lesson.title: Review Day: Reading a Chapter Book
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: This week you read a whole 3-chapter story. Let's review everything you learned!

Quick review: a chapter book tells its story in parts you read one at a time (Day 1). A character trait comes from what someone does, not just how they feel (Day 2). Retelling a story in order uses first/then/finally (Day 3). Context clues help you figure out tricky words (Day 4). Answer: what is one character trait Mira showed, and what clue from the story tells you a word's meaning?
Wonderful work this week — you read a whole chapter-book-style story and used 4 real reading skills! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review chapter-book structure, character traits, sequencing, and context clues
Recall one character trait and one context-clue example from this week's story
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child answer both review questions.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of chapter-book reading!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one of the two review questions, whichever the child engaged with most this week
Ready for more: ask the child what they think might happen if there were a Chapter 4 to this story
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four reading skills needs the most reinforcement before the next chapter-book unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and review activity — check that the child can name a real character trait Mira showed (brave/kind) and correctly explain how context clues helped figure out 'gripped.'
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 3 Reading and Language standards (RL.3.1/RL.3.3/RL.3.5, L.3.4a) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
